messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a new pattern: lots of tiny ephemeral pods (0.25-0.5 GPU) landing everywhere and leaving node 'shelves' full of 1-2 token fragments. Large batch jobs can't binpack. Stranded GPUs ~17% in eu-west1 last 6h.
ajay: Can you paste the eviction/scheduler logs? curious which predicate is failing.
maria: sure, snippet:
```
I0320 14:12:01.123 kube-scheduler fit failed: Insufficient gpu
I0320 14:12:01.124 kube-scheduler predicate didn't match: PodAntiAffinity
I0320 14:12:02.200 kube-scheduler Preemption: needed 4 GPUs found 1 free
```
sam: Ugh. sounds like micro-pods are causing fragmentation, not taints. do we have a tiny-pod QPS burst in EU? :eyes: 
maria: yes, spike correlates with nightly batch of onboarding tests from staging hitting eu-west1 at 02:00 UTC.
ryan: short-term: label nodes for tiny-pods -> schedule them to a special pool. mid-term: change scheduler scoring to prefer packing by (gpuAllocatable - gpuRequested) or add a binpacking plugin. also consider a small-pod admission hint.
ajay: descheduler could help remove tiny pods from scattered nodes using LowNodeUtilization, but risk churn + evictions. need throttling and chaos window.
infra-bot: alert: cluster/eu-west1/gpu_utilization_stranded > 15% (6h average)
maria: action items: 1) create 'tiny-pod-pool' node group and add nodeLabel, 2) add admission rule to recommend nodeSelector for pods requesting <0.5 GPU (opt-in), 3) enable a canary descheduler run on non-prod for 2h, 4) dashboard and alert tile. I'll open a runbook PR.
sam: cost note — consolidating reduces long-tail node counts (saves ~0.12 GPU-hours/minute) but could increase tail latency for tiny jobs; quantify with perf test. :thumbsup: 
ryan: +1. Also let's throttle autoscaler bursts for eu-west1 for the next 24h to avoid creating more small nodes.
ajay: I'll schedule a quick test at 16:00 UTC to label 3 nodes and migrate 20 pods. who can verify metrics?
maria: I'll watch Grafana, ping me in #eng-oncall if it spikes. :eyes: 
sam: thanks — sounds good.
